name: Online tutor (languages and other subjects)
summary: Set your own rate and teach one-on-one video lessons on the Preply marketplace; Preply keeps the whole first trial lesson with each new student and 18–33% of later lessons.
whatYouDo: You build a profile with a photo and intro video, set your price and availability, and teach booked one-on-one lessons (English, French, other languages or subjects). Income depends on attracting and keeping students in a crowded marketplace.
appeal: You set your own price and schedule
Can teach English, French or other languages and subjects
No teaching certificate required (per third-party guides)
Commission falls as you accumulate hours taught (33% down to 18%)
watchOuts: Preply keeps 100% of every trial lesson with a new student, so first lessons are effectively unpaid
33% commission for new tutors; 18% only after 400+ hours taught
Crowded marketplace (one review cites 12,000+ English tutors), making first students hard to get
Complaint-board reports of tutor profiles removed without warning (individual, unverified)
Income is unpredictable, especially early on

compensation.notes: Tutors set their own rates. Official commission example: on a $10/hour lesson a new tutor keeps $6.70 and a tutor with 400+ hours keeps $8.20 (non-trial lessons).

reliability.notes: Earnings depend entirely on student bookings; no guaranteed volume. Large tutor supply reported.

fees: Commission: 100% of each trial lesson with a new student; 33% of regular lessons for new tutors, falling (28% after 20 hours per secondary sources) to 18% at 400+ hours (official help article).
applicationSteps: Sign up on Preply's teach page and create a tutor profile
Add a photo, short intro video, description and availability
Set your price and take trial lessons (first lesson with each new student is not paid to you)
fitsIf: You can teach a language (including French) or subject, enjoy live video teaching, and are willing to market yourself to build a student base.
notFitIf: You need income within days or dislike giving away first lessons and competing on price.

sources.title: Teach online: Become an online tutor at Preply
sources.notes: Official tutor recruitment page (seen in search results; not opened). Search summary attributes the trial 100% / 33%→18% commission statement to it.

sources.title: Preply commission model
sources.notes: Help article: 100% commission on each trial lesson with a new student; non-trial commission starts at 33% and drops to 18% with hours taught; $10/h example (keep $6.70 new, $8.20 at 400+ hours).

sources.title: Preply Review: Is It Any Good For Online Teachers?
sources.notes: Review noting 12,000+ English tutors at time of writing (hard to stand out) and student complaints about subscription pricing.

sources.title: Preply complaints
sources.notes: Complaint posts including a tutor profile deleted without warning; individual, unverified reports.

sources.title: Becoming a Preply Tutor: Pay, Requirements and an Honest Look
sources.notes: Third-party guide. Search summaries of guides say no teaching certificate is needed, profile review takes ~3–5 working days and no country restriction on tutors is stated (not pinned to this page).
